title: Intent-Based Interaction Evaluation Framework
description: Framework for evaluating systems where interfaces are dynamically generated from user intent. Based on Jakob Nielsen's vision of 'No More User Interface' where AI agents generate interfaces on the fly.

thought_leader.name: Jakob Nielsen
thought_leader.key_insight: Traditional GUI will be replaced by AI agents that generate interfaces on the fly based on user intent
thought_leader.implication: We evaluate intent capture and outcome delivery, not static interface elements

paradigm_shift.from: User navigates pre-designed interface to accomplish task
paradigm_shift.to: User expresses intent, system generates appropriate interface/response

evaluation_dimensions.name: Intent Capture Fidelity
evaluation_dimensions.description: How accurately does the system understand what the user wants to accomplish?
key_aspects: Scope capture - understanding the full extent of the request
Nuance recognition - picking up on subtle requirements
Context integration - using situational context appropriately
Ambiguity handling - resolving unclear requests gracefully

questions: Does the system capture the full scope of user intent?
Are ambiguities resolved through clarification, not assumption?
Is implicit intent (context, history, patterns) appropriately factored?
Can the user refine intent iteratively without starting over?
what_to_look_for: Intent disambiguation mechanisms that ask smart questions
Context-aware intent inference using history and situation
Intent history and pattern recognition
Clarification dialogue that narrows without frustrating
anti_patterns: Assuming instead of asking when ambiguous
Ignoring context that would clarify intent
Requiring complete, perfect specification upfront
Losing partial intent when user refines

metrics.name: intent_match_accuracy
metrics.description: How often interpreted intent matches actual user intent

metrics.name: implicit_intent_detection_rate
metrics.description: Successfully inferring unstated but important intent
metrics.example: User asks for 'meeting notes' - system knows to include action items

evaluation_dimensions.name: Interface Generation Appropriateness
evaluation_dimensions.description: Is the dynamically generated interface optimal for the expressed intent?
key_aspects: Complexity matching - interface complexity matches task complexity
Modality selection - choosing the right form of interaction
Progressive generation - building interface as understanding grows
Minimalism - eliminating unnecessary interface elements

questions: Does the generated interface match the complexity of the task?
Is the interface modality appropriate (visual, conversational, mixed)?
Does the interface adapt as intent evolves?
Is unnecessary interface eliminated for simple intents?
what_to_look_for: Simple tasks get simple interfaces (or no interface)
Complex tasks get appropriately structured interfaces
Modality selection logic is appropriate to task
Real-time interface adaptation as needs become clearer
anti_patterns: Same heavyweight interface for all task types
Forcing visual interface when conversational would suffice
Static interface that doesn't adapt to evolving intent
Unnecessary choices and options for simple tasks

when_inappropriate: Information that fits in a sentence

when_appropriate: Complex tasks with both information gathering and comparison
Tasks that benefit from both explanation and visualization

metrics.name: interface_appropriateness_score
metrics.description: User rating of interface fit for task

metrics.name: modality_match_rate
metrics.description: How often chosen modality matches user preference

metrics.name: adaptation_responsiveness
metrics.description: Speed and smoothness of interface adaptation

evaluation_dimensions.name: Intent-Outcome Continuity
evaluation_dimensions.description: Is there a clear, traceable path from expressed intent to delivered outcome?
key_aspects: Traceability - user can follow intent to outcome
Transparency - understanding of how intent was interpreted
Intervention - ability to correct course during execution
Alignment - outcome clearly maps to original intent

questions: Can users understand how their intent led to the outcome?
Are intermediate steps visible when needed?
Can users intervene at any point in the intent-to-outcome flow?
Is the outcome clearly connected to the original intent?
what_to_look_for: Intent-outcome traceability on demand
Progressive disclosure of process (summary first, detail on demand)
Clear intervention points during execution
Outcome presentation that references original intent
anti_patterns: Black box processing with surprise outcomes
No explanation of how intent became outcome
No ability to stop or redirect during processing
Outcomes that don't obviously relate to intent

metrics.name: traceability_score
metrics.description: User can explain how intent led to outcome

evaluation_dimensions.name: Zero-Interface Opportunities
evaluation_dimensions.description: When is NO interface the right answer?
key_aspects: Proactive automation - acting without being asked when appropriate
Background processing - handling tasks silently
Notification vs. interaction - informing without requiring action
Appropriate scope - knowing when zero-interface is safe

questions: Can outcomes be delivered without any interface?
Does the system proactively accomplish things without requiring interaction?
Are routine decisions automated appropriately?
Is the user appropriately notified of background actions?
what_to_look_for: Proactive automation of routine, low-risk tasks
Appropriate boundaries on what's automated
Transparent notification of background actions
Easy override when automation isn't wanted
anti_patterns: Requiring interaction for completely predictable actions
Hiding automation when user should know
Automating high-stakes decisions without safeguards
No way to disable unwanted automation

metrics.name: automation_appropriateness
metrics.description: User would have done the same thing

metrics.name: zero_interface_success_rate
metrics.description: Background actions that needed no correction

evaluation_dimensions.name: Intent Evolution Support
evaluation_dimensions.description: How well does the system support evolving and changing user intent?
key_aspects: Mid-stream changes - adjusting intent during interaction
Scope expansion - adding to original intent
Scope reduction - narrowing focus
Complete pivots - changing direction entirely

questions: Can users change their intent mid-interaction without starting over?
Does partial work persist when intent evolves?
Is intent history available for reference?
Can users branch from previous intents?
what_to_look_for: Graceful handling of 'actually, I meant...' moments
Preservation of useful work when intent shifts
Intent history and branching support
Natural language intent modification
anti_patterns: Forcing restart when intent changes
Losing all progress on intent modification
No memory of previous intent attempts
Rigid interpretation that can't flex

metrics.name: work_preservation_rate
metrics.description: Useful work preserved when intent changes

evaluation_methodology.instead_of: Walk through interface screens evaluating each against heuristics

do_this.action: Express a range of user intents at different complexity levels
examples: Moderate: 'Plan a trip to Paris next month'
Complex: 'Help me prepare for a job interview at a tech company'

do_this.action: Evaluate how system captures, interprets, and responds to each intent
Assess whether generated interfaces were appropriate or could be eliminated
criteria: Could a simpler interaction have sufficed?
How direct was the path from intent to outcome?

do_this.action: Test intent refinement and correction flows
criteria: How gracefully did the system handle changes?
Could the user redirect without frustration?

levels.label: Excellent Intent Handling
levels.description: Intent perfectly captured, optimal interface generated, seamless flow to outcome

levels.label: Good Intent Handling
levels.description: Minor clarification needed, appropriate interface, clear path to outcome

levels.label: Adequate Intent Handling
levels.description: Some misinterpretation, interface slightly mismatched, outcome achieved with effort

levels.label: Poor Intent Handling
levels.description: Significant misinterpretation, inappropriate interface, difficult path to outcome

levels.label: Failed Intent Handling
levels.description: Intent not captured, wrong interface, user cannot achieve intended outcome
